standard: ISO 26262:2018 Part 3 §6 — Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment
scope: rust-MQTT as a Safety Element Out Of Context (SEOOC). System-level HARA to be performed by the integrating application for its specific operational context.
item_definition: rust-MQTT is a pure-Rust MQTT client library providing publish/subscribe messaging over TCP for safety-critical vehicle signal routing. It is used in vehicle network gateways and COVESA VISSR implementations.
severity_scale: S0=No injury, S1=Light/moderate injury, S2=Severe injury (survival probable), S3=Life-threatening (survival uncertain) — per ISO 26262 Part 3 Table 1
exposure_scale: E0=Incredibly unlikely, E1=Very low, E2=Low, E3=Medium, E4=High — per ISO 26262 Part 3 Table 2
controllability_scale: C0=Controllable in general, C1=Simply controllable, C2=Normally controllable, C3=Difficult to control — per ISO 26262 Part 3 Table 3
asil_determination: ISO 26262 Part 3 Table 4: S x E x C matrix

hazards.name: Message Loss
hazards.description: An MQTT message carrying a safety-critical vehicle signal (brake-by-wire command, ADAS alert) is not delivered due to library error

hazards.name: Message Corruption
hazards.description: An MQTT message payload or topic is silently modified before delivery, causing the receiving subsystem to act on incorrect data

hazards.name: Topic Misrouting
hazards.description: A message is delivered to the wrong subscriber due to incorrect wildcard matching, causing unintended actuation

hazards.name: Stale Message Delivered
hazards.description: A retained message with an expired timestamp is delivered to a new subscriber, causing action on outdated vehicle state

hazards.name: Connection Blackout
hazards.description: The library enters a silently disconnected state while reporting as connected, causing all messages to be lost without indication

hazards.name: System Hang
hazards.description: A subscriber task deadlocks or blocks permanently due to back-pressure failure, causing loss of vehicle signal monitoring

hazardous_events.operational_situation: High-speed highway driving (> 100 km/h), vehicle approaching obstacle
hazardous_events.hazardous_event: Brake-by-wire MQTT command lost; vehicle does not decelerate
hazardous_events.exposure_rationale: High-speed driving occurs frequently for vehicles with automated driving features
hazardous_events.controllability_rationale: Driver may not be monitoring for automated brake failure; reaction time insufficient at speed
hazardous_events.asil_rationale: S3 x E4 x C3 → ASIL-D per ISO 26262 Part 3 Table 4
hazardous_events.note: ASIL-D exceeds this library's ASIL-B rating. System integrator MUST NOT use rust-MQTT as sole path for brake-by-wire commands without additional ASIL-D redundancy at system level.
hazardous_events.safety_goal: SG-001: rust-MQTT shall not be used as the sole communication path for ASIL-D functions without system-level redundancy

hazardous_events.operational_situation: Normal driving, ADAS collision warning active
hazardous_events.hazardous_event: ADAS hazard alert MQTT message lost; driver not warned of imminent collision
hazardous_events.exposure_rationale: Collision situations occur with medium frequency for ADAS-equipped vehicles
hazardous_events.controllability_rationale: Driver may be able to observe hazard directly and react
hazardous_events.asil_rationale: S2 x E3 x C2 → ASIL-B per ISO 26262 Part 3 Table 4
hazardous_events.safety_goal: SG-002: Message delivery shall be reliable; QoS ≥ 1 shall be used for safety-relevant ADAS signals

hazardous_events.operational_situation: Multiple vehicle subsystems sharing MQTT broker
hazardous_events.hazardous_event: Throttle command routed to brake subsystem subscriber due to topic wildcard mismatch
hazardous_events.exposure_rationale: Multi-subsystem MQTT deployment is the primary use case
hazardous_events.controllability_rationale: Incorrect actuation provides no warning; driver cannot anticipate
hazardous_events.asil_rationale: S3 x E4 x C3 → ASIL-D
hazardous_events.note: As for HE-001, system integrator must use topic naming conventions that prevent single wildcard expressions from spanning safety and non-safety domains.
hazardous_events.safety_goal: SG-003: Topic namespaces for safety-critical and non-safety signals shall be segregated; rust-MQTT wildcard matching shall exactly follow MQTT §4.7

hazardous_events.operational_situation: Vehicle startup; subsystem subscribing to retrieve last known state
hazardous_events.hazardous_event: Stale retained message (e.g. 5-minute-old sensor reading) delivered at startup; system acts on outdated value
hazardous_events.exposure_rationale: Startup occurs regularly; retained messages always delivered on subscribe
hazardous_events.controllability_rationale: Systems typically verify freshness, but not always automated
hazardous_events.asil_rationale: S1 x E3 x C2 → ASIL-A
hazardous_events.safety_goal: SG-004: Integrators shall use expiry_interval on retained safety signals; rust-MQTT shall preserve expiry_interval across the RELAY layer

hazardous_events.operational_situation: High-throughput signal bus; subscriber slow to consume
hazardous_events.hazardous_event: Subscriber channel full; back-pressure policy not applied; async task blocks indefinitely
hazardous_events.exposure_rationale: High-throughput signal bursts are common in vehicle networks (e.g. radar point clouds)
hazardous_events.controllability_rationale: Application may detect task silence and restart, but not guaranteed
hazardous_events.asil_rationale: S2 x E3 x C2 → ASIL-B
hazardous_events.safety_goal: SG-005: rust-MQTT shall enforce configured back-pressure policy; no subscriber channel shall block the publisher task

hazardous_events.operational_situation: Continuous vehicle monitoring; TCP connection silently dropped by network
hazardous_events.hazardous_event: Library reports healthy but CONNACK was rejected; all publishes silently discarded
hazardous_events.exposure_rationale: Network interruptions occur in vehicle environments (tunnels, RF interference)
hazardous_events.controllability_rationale: Application may implement watchdog; not automatic
hazardous_events.asil_rationale: S2 x E3 x C2 → ASIL-B
hazardous_events.safety_goal: SG-006: rust-MQTT shall validate CONNACK return code and return Error::ConnectionRefused on rejection; integrators shall implement reconnect logic

safety_goals.description: rust-MQTT shall not be used as the sole communication path for ASIL-D functions without system-level redundancy
Message delivery shall be reliable; QoS ≥ 1 shall be used for safety-relevant signals
Topic namespaces for safety-critical and non-safety signals shall be segregated
Integrators shall use expiry_interval on retained safety signals
No subscriber channel shall block the publisher task; back-pressure must be configured
Integrators shall implement reconnect logic and monitor CONNACK validation
